recipes.name: 3-Cheese Pasta Bake
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup (Regular, 98% Fat Free or 25% Less Sodium)

steps.text: Mix soup, cheeses, milk and black pepper in 1 1/2-qt. casserole. Stir in pasta.
Bake at 400 degrees F. for 20 min. or until hot.

raw_recipe.headline: 3-Cheese Pasta Bake
raw_recipe.description: Tender corkscrew pasta is cloaked in a creamy mushroom sauce sporting flavors of three cheeses.

review.reviewBody:
Yum! I was worried it would be taste just of mushrooms, but I was pleasantly surprised. I used cheddar and pepper jack cheese with a couple dashes of hot sauce, because I love bold flavors. This is my mistake, but I didn't know what four cups of cooked pasta would be, so I just cooked a pound of pasta, which ended up being too much. Next time will measure like I should!

EDIT: I made this again, measured correctly, and used cheese soup instead of mushroom. I will definitely use the cheese soup again, it just gives it a little something extra.

This actually wasn't too bad, just made, based on what I had in the house. It is on the salty side, from the canned soup and the amount of cheese. It kind of has a slight alfredo sauce flavor from the parmesan cheese. I only had about 3/4 of a cup of cheddar blend cheese left, so I used 1 1/4 cups of fresh grated mozzarella for the rest. The footnotes say to use 2 cups of cheese. I made sure to boil the pasta very well, so it did not soak up too much of the cheese sauce in the oven and dry out. I even took it out 2-3 minutes early. I was also concerned about it sticking to my baking pan, but it didn't at all after spraying the pan lightly with PAM. I recommend measuring the pasta after boiling as I found that I only ended up needing about 1/2 the bag of the 1 lb cooked bag to equal the 4 cups. It didn't make a lot, but I still ended up with some leftovers that never got eaten for some reason.

I did not have two cheese blend so I just picked two cheeses (sharp cheddar, longhorn style colby), shredded them and used those. After stirring what I had grated into the rest of the ingredients, I did add another cup or so. I didn't really measure, I just kind of guessed and threw in. As with any cheesy dish, I added my own personal touches (squirt dijon, little Frank's Hot Sauce, onion/garlic powder) and I threw in about a cup and a half of blanched broccoli. This was very easy and there were no leftovers. This could be easily adapted to any condensed soup you have on hand. Next time, I might try this with Cream of Chicken or Cheddar Cheese soup.

I added crushed Ritz Crackers to the ingredients and used 8 oz. of Mozzarella, 1/3 cup of cheddar, and 1/2 cup of parmesan. I mixed everything in a bowl before putting in the casserole dish. When there were only 5 minutes of bake time left, I layered the top of the casserole with crushed Ritz crackers. The husband could not stop eating it. This is definitely a new favorite and so simple to make. LOVE!

This was much better than I expected, although I did make a few changes to fit our lifestyle. For one, I used Health Valley mushroom soup, which is not condensed, so I only used 1/2 cup milk. I also added some steamed broccoli and onion we had on hand and threw some bread crumbs and paprika on the top just for kicks. The broccoli was a GREAT addition. But cheers for a creamy pasta recipe that was tasty and not runny! Family loved it.

I too had to tweak, to use up what I had, and this recipe seemed to be tweakable. I sautéed two onions and a 4 oz can of mushrooms with some garlic. Used 1 lb Scoobidoo noodles for fun, 1 can c. of broccoli and two cups milk, 1 T Italian seasoning and some black and cayenne pepper. I also threw in a handful of beans the kids brought in from the garden; I steamed these first though. My cheese mix was cheddar-mozz. I also had a rib steak left over from last night, so I diced that and added it. The whole thing fit nicely in a 9x13 pan. The result was creamy and flavourful, a great casserole and the kids just loved it, but I think all the additions I made helped the flavour a great deal. I'd call this a base recipe, and add your odds and ends as I did for a great casserole meal.

This recipe is easy to make and turns out so creamy. I use cream of chicken instead of mushroom and I add chicken and bacon bits and just a little bit more milk since the chicken soaks up a lot of the juice. It’s like macaroni and cheese mixed with chicken and dumplings. Sooo good.

This is a great base recipe to add protein and/or veggies to in order to make it a hearty main dish. I followed a few other reviewers’ recommendations to swap the condensed cream of mushroom soup for condensed cheddar cheese soup, and that was a great choice. I also seasoned to taste (some salt and garlic powder in addition to the pepper). I tossed in some shredded rotisserie chicken when serving, and it was great. I could see this being great with tuna or ground beef as well, and I think broccoli could be a delicious addition. Even without the add-ins, it was saucy and creamy and could make a great side dish as-is (just remember to season to taste).

This is an exceptional dish. I usually make recipes the first time exactly the way it is written. However, this was adjusted out of necessity. My grandson said he does not like mushrooms so 
I used Broccoli Cheese soup. I misread the instructions and used a total of 4 1/3 cups of cheese. I added some mixed veggies and broccoli with cheese sauce to the soup/cheese mix as well some cooked shrimp. I did not bake it but sat it on low fire till it was heated through. I know it was good as that picky 6 year-old ate it well. I will be making again and this time like the recipe reads.

I used this recipe as a base. Instead of mushroom or the cheese soup, I used cream of asparagusm yummy.Then I added gloves of garlic, onion powder, garlic powder, cooking herb and garlic cream cheese a little dry mustard. added with the milk and cheese, blended it all together with some fresh vegies and topped with fresh parm. I made it as written a few times and loved it as well, just decided to dress it up a bit.

just got done eating this really simple delicious dish. i read all the reviews wanted to go with the cheese soup, but the store i went to only had the cream of mushroom. i grilled some chicken breast and added it to the mix before we baked it. it was simply amazing.
I think my family will love this dish when I make it up with 3 different types of cheeses in the dish and having it baked as well.

I made this with cream of chicken soup because I had no cream of mushroom soup. I used Armstrong Farmer’s and Pizza Mozzarella cheese with smoked bacon because that’s what I had. I used pasta shells because that’s what I had. I added a a few shakes of Worcestershire sauce because I thought that would be yummy. Added a salad for health purposes. 😬 It was sooo yummy!!
Very easy and tasty.

This was so easy and delicious to make. I've used generic cream of mushroom soup instead of Campbell's (still tasted good) and a combo of shredded cheddar and mozzarella cheeses. I would love to try other combos when I make it again. I wish I didn't use more than 2 cups since a third of the pasta were hard to eat.
I made this by the recipe. I did add 1/4 tsp. of dry minced garlic for more robust flavor. Also sprinkled top with Sweet Paprika for added color.

I first tried this when I was in high school a couple of years ago, everyone loved it in my nutrition wellness class. The only thing I changed was instead of chream of mushroom I added cream of chicken. I make it a lot and it is still so good. easy to make also which is a plus.
Just ok...
Perfect as is. I triple the recipe for my family because we have 6 kids and want leftovers.
Amazingly delicious!
